name: VA Tech Wabag Ltd
tagline: Asset-light water-treatment EPC + O&M with an improving return profile and a Rs 19,400 Cr order book -- a solid compounder, but at ~Rs 13,500 Cr too large for a 10x/100x thesis
business_overview: VA Tech Wabag designs, builds and operates drinking-water, waste-water, industrial-water and desalination plants in India and internationally, on an asset-light EPC-plus-O&M model.
fundamentals_table: Q1 FY27 revenue +20.8% YoY, PAT +37% YoY
~Rs 19,400 Cr (~4x revenue), boosted by wins in Kuwait, UAE and Vienna
Targeting ~20% revenue growth and ~15% EBITDA margin
fundamentals_narrative: A genuinely improving business: ROCE moving toward 20%+, ROE ~14% versus a 5-yr average of ~11%, ~21% recent revenue growth and a record order book at ~4x revenue. The model is asset-light. The constraint is size -- from ~Rs 13,500 Cr, a 10x in 2-3 years or 100x in 10 years is not a realistic outcome for an EPC-style water company growing ~20%.
technical_read: Not pulled -- filtered on size. Stock up ~42% over the year.
sentiment_summary: Not deep-read this pass. Filtered at the preliminary stage on size: a good-quality, ~20%-growth mid/large-cap with a strong order book is a solid compounder but not a multi-bagger candidate, and the large-cap recent-inflection carve-out does not apply.
community_signal: Not assessed this pass (active thread of ~137 replies, but the size call makes a deep dive unnecessary).
bull_case: Improving returns (ROCE toward 20%+) on an asset-light EPC + O&M model
Record order book ~Rs 19,400 Cr (~4x revenue) with strong international wins
bear_case: ~Rs 13,470 Cr market cap -- a 10x/100x outcome is unrealistic
EPC-style revenue with execution and working-capital risk
~20% growth needs to be sustained and re-rated to move the needle
verdict_headline: A quality, improving water-treatment compounder -- but too large for the thesis; filtered out on size
verdict_reasoning: The business is genuinely good and improving, which is why it was screened, but from ~Rs 13,500 Cr and ~20% growth a 10x/100x outcome is not realistic
No red flag, but size rules it out -> 'neither'; conviction Low-to-Medium on quality; no revisit (size gate)
disclaimer: This is independent research for informational purposes only, not investment advice.
